newsitem.title: USA: Levitt sees need for more funds in advisers' role.
newsitem.headline: Levitt sees need for more funds in advisers' role.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission will need more funding, should Congress require it to step up oversight of investment advisers, a function it currently can not cope with because of "woefully inadequate" funds, SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt said on Friday.

Levitt made his agency's position clear in a letter to Rep. Thomas Bliley, the Virginia Republican who chairs the House Commerce Committee and who is pushing for enactment of a securities bill within the current congressional term.
Levitt said,"our resources are woefully inadequate to protect the millions of American investors who depend on the services of investment advisers."
He noted that the SEC now examines smaller investment firms at an average of once every 44 years, "which is tantamount to no examination at all."
Levitt sent the letter even as House and Senate negotiators were still at loggerheads over the bill's provisions governing the investment advisory industry.
Senate proponents led by Texas Republican Phil Gramm want the SEC to shoulder greater responsibility in licensing and regulating investment advisory firms with more than $25 million in assets.

Negotiators in the House, including ranking Democrats in the Commerce Committee, initially wanted to allow state regulators to oversee the nation's 150,000 investment advisers, but later said they would be willing to go along with Gramm provided the SEC got additional funding. The House negotiators also asked that the advisers be required to comply with additional disclosure and other rules.

Legislative aides said Gramm is unwilling to grant the SEC additional funding, a position he has espoused in the past. No breakthrough had been reached on the issue as of early Friday evening, the aides added.
